response:
Diagnosis. The archive has converged on a clear champion family and gen-6 sharpened the picture. Best joint evidence: pre-issuance-scaled dilution (fmb −2.20, alpha −4.8%, Sharpe −0.374) and revenue-scaled dilution (fmb −2.27, alpha −4.4%, Sharpe −0.364), both with coverage of only ~0.061 because they require a fourth year of history. Best alpha and Sharpe in the whole archive came from the bounded shareholder-funded-share leg (alpha −6.9%, t=−3.79, Sharpe −0.384) but with a zero slope, which now looks like a moderator effect: legs paired with the wcap/at channel give big alphas and no slope, legs paired with oancf/lct give reliable slopes and −4 to −5% alphas. Two failures also inform: moderators built from *stock-of-deficit* type variables (re level, re trend, txt/sale, accrual gap) repeatedly deliver slopes with wrong-signed or null alphas, so the productive distress axis is short-horizon funding capacity, not cumulative damage. This batch therefore (i) fixes the champion's coverage penalty with a self-referential pre-issuance base, (ii) tests a single economic coverage ratio as moderator instead of a two-rank sum, (iii) builds the dependence measure as a genuine cumulative financing gap, and (iv) opens two new axes — working-capital bloat and internal debt-service self-sufficiency — with the last providing the long-side evidence the archive still lacks.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Dilution against the internally funded asset base
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(sstk, 3), SUB(at, TS_SUM(sstk, 3)))), SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(che, lct)), NEG(RATIO(oancf, lct))))
HYPOTHESIS: Dependence on outside equity is the ratio of what shareholders have recently injected to the part of the firm that was not built with those injections; firms whose recent raises rival or exceed their internally funded asset base are running on investor capital, and this is priced most sharply when current liabilities cannot be covered.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: This achieves the same denominator-endogeneity fix as the champion's LAG(at, 3) base — proceeds are removed from the scaler rather than avoided by looking backwards — but requires no fourth year of history, so it should restore coverage from 0.062 toward 0.079 while preserving the reordering of the heaviest diluters. Coverage was the explicit caveat on the archive's strongest signal, and fixing it without changing the moderator keeps attribution clean.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Dilution against cash coverage of current liabilities
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(sstk, 3), at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(che, oancf), lct))))
HYPOTHESIS: The distress state that makes repeated dilution costly is simply that cash on hand plus this year's operating cash flow fall short of current obligations; expressed as one coverage ratio rather than two separately ranked channels, this state should identify the vulnerable firms more faithfully.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Every strong archive signal has used a two-channel SUMRANK moderator, which imposes equal rank weights on ratios of very different economic content and discards the level information in each; combining the stock and the flow in the numerator of a single coverage ratio is a different measurement decision, not a channel swap. Because the two-rank moderators split cleanly into "alpha channels" (wcap/at) and "slope channels" (oancf/lct), testing a unified coverage quantity is the natural way to find out whether one construct can deliver both.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Equity funding an operating working-capital bloat
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(sstk, 3), at)), RANK(GROWTH(RATIO(SUB(act, che), sale), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: When a serial equity issuer's non-cash current assets are growing faster than its sales, the money raised is being absorbed by uncollected receivables and unsold inventory rather than by productive investment, which signals deteriorating operations and the likelihood of further dilution.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Operating working-capital efficiency is an entirely new distress axis for this archive and it is conceptually independent of the funding-capacity ratios that have dominated: it asks where the money went in the operating cycle, not whether obligations can be met. It also gives a specific, testable use-of-proceeds mechanism that the earlier one-year change-in-cash test could not capture, since inventory and receivable bloat is exactly how proceeds disappear without cash ever appearing on the balance sheet.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Internal coverage of debt amortization under illiquidity
EXPRESSION: MUL(ZSCORE(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(TS_SUM(oancf, 3), TS_SUM(dltr, 3)), 2))), SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(che, lct)), NEG(RATIO(wcap, at))))
HYPOTHESIS: Among firms with no liquidity buffer, those whose three-year operating cash flow comfortably covers the debt they have had to repay are servicing their obligations from the business itself and are far less fragile than their balance sheets suggest, so they should earn positive abnormal returns relative to illiquid firms that cannot cover amortization internally.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This is the archive's first long-side construct built on debt-service capacity rather than on payout behaviour, and centering the leg means the illiquidity moderator amplifies both tails symmetrically instead of imposing its own negative main effect — the defect that sank the earlier repurchase and dividend-retrenchment tests. It directly complements signal 1: one measures dependence on shareholders, the other self-sufficiency against creditors, and together they establish whether the mechanism is symmetric or purely short-side.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Recent dilution relative to the equity claim
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(sstk, 3), ABS(ceq))), SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(che, lct)), NEG(RATIO(oancf, lct))))
HYPOTHESIS: What matters to an existing shareholder is what fraction of the current equity claim was purchased by new investors in the last three years; when that fraction is large and the firm cannot cover its current liabilities, the incumbent claim is being progressively transferred to successive rounds of new buyers.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Assets and revenue scalers measure dependence from the firm's perspective, whereas the book equity base measures it from the incumbent shareholder's perspective, and for highly levered or asset-light firms these differ sharply — a firm can raise little relative to assets yet a great deal relative to its thin equity. Using the absolute value keeps negative-book-equity firms at the informative extreme instead of flipping them to the long side, which is the correct economic ordering for a distress study.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Cumulative financing gap under liquidity deficit
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(TS_SUM(sstk, 3), TS_SUM(oancf, 3)), SUB(at, TS_SUM(sstk, 3)))), SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(che, lct)), NEG(RATIO(wcap, at))))
HYPOTHESIS: The economically complete measure of external dependence is equity raised net of cash generated internally over the same window: a firm that raised heavily but also generated cash is not dependent, whereas one that raised heavily while burning cash has a genuine financing gap, and that gap is dangerous where working capital is already negative.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The bounded shareholder-funded-share construct produced the archive's largest alpha (−6.9%) but no slope, plausibly because the bounded transform compresses exactly the extreme burners it is meant to identify; expressing the same economics as a signed difference over a non-financed asset base preserves the ordering of severe gaps and should recover the cross-sectional slope while retaining the alpha. Both the numerator and the denominator now embed the cross-theme interaction, making this the most integrated version of the dependence mechanism tested so far.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---CRITIQUE Dilution against the internally funded asset base---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: For r = TS_SUM(sstk,3)/at < 1 the expression r/(1−r) is a strictly monotone transform of r, so after RANK this is rank-identical to the already-tested gen-2 "Serial dilution with chronic cash shortfall" (same moderator), and the only cases where it differs — r ≥ 1, precisely the heaviest diluters the hypothesis targets — flip to large negative values and land on the *long* side, contradicting the stated sign.

---CRITIQUE Dilution against cash coverage of current liabilities---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: This is the gen-2 dilution signal with the two-channel SUMRANK moderator collapsed into a single ranked coverage ratio built from the same two inputs (che, oancf, lct) — a defensible but essentially cosmetic re-weighting of an already-tested moderator, with little chance of a mechanistically new result.

---CRITIQUE Equity funding an operating working-capital bloat---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The use-of-proceeds-in-the-operating-cycle axis is genuinely new for this archive and the interaction is coherent, but it overlaps substantially with the working-capital accrual anomaly (Sloan) and with the already-failed gen-5 "cash-poor earnings" test, and GROWTH of a sales-scaled ratio is unstable for exactly the low- or zero-revenue serial diluters the signal is meant to identify.

---CRITIQUE Internal coverage of debt amortization under illiquidity---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: A legitimately new long-side construct (debt-service self-sufficiency rather than payout behaviour) with the centering fix correctly motivated by prior failures, though the oancf/dltr ratio is fragile where dltr is near zero — firms with no amortization schedule score as "infinitely covered" and will dominate the long leg for reasons unrelated to the hypothesis.

---CRITIQUE Recent dilution relative to the equity claim---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This is the fourth scaler swap in an otherwise unchanged issuance × illiquidity family (at, LAG(at,3), LAG(sale,3), now |ceq|), sstk/ceq is close to standard book-scaled issuance measures already documented in the literature, and ABS(ceq) creates a blow-up at ceq ≈ 0 that pools economically opposite states into the same extreme.

---CRITIQUE Cumulative financing gap under liquidity deficit---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: The signed financing-gap numerator is a reasonable idea (though close to the published net-external-financing anomaly already probed in generation 0), but it is paired with the same SUB(at, TS_SUM(sstk,3)) denominator whose sign flips near zero, so the severest gap cases — the whole point of abandoning the bounded transform — get mis-ordered rather than preserved.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Serial dilution with near-term debt overhang
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(sstk, 3), at)), RANK(RATIO(dlc, act)))
HYPOTHESIS: A firm that has repeatedly sold equity and also carries debt maturing within the year that is large relative to its entire current asset base faces a hard deadline: the next repayment must be met from a new raise, so its bargaining position with investors is at its weakest and returns should be poor.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
REASONING: Every moderator tested so far measures obligations in aggregate (current liabilities, working capital, cash flow coverage); this one measures the *maturity* of the claim that is about to come due against liquid resources, which is the specific state that forces dilution on the issuer's terms rather than the firm's. Both legs are stable, always-positive ratios with no sign-flip or blow-up risk, and the debt-overhang leg is not a rescaling of anything in the archive, so the test is about a new distress state rather than a new denominator.

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Dependence meeting a fresh collapse in funding capacity
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(sstk, 3), at)), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(ADD(che, oancf), lct), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: A history of dilution becomes actionable news when funding capacity suddenly deteriorates: firms whose cash-plus-operating-flow coverage of current liabilities has just fallen sharply are the ones about to return to the market, and the timing of that deterioration is what the market is slow to price.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
REASONING: This pairs a slow-moving dependence state with a one-year shock to funding capacity rather than with another level of distress, so it tests timing rather than intensity — an axis on which the archive has only one weak observation (gen-1's one-year financing escalation against coverage deterioration, which used a noisy one-year financing leg). Because the shock leg is a signed change while the dependence leg is a cumulative state, the two legs carry genuinely different information and neither is a monotone transform of any evaluated signal.

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Self-funding ratio under liquidity stress
EXPRESSION: MUL(ZSCORE(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(TS_SUM(oancf, 3), ADD(TS_SUM(sstk, 3), TS_SUM(dltis, 3))), 2))), SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(che, lct)), NEG(RATIO(wcap, at))))
HYPOTHESIS: Among firms whose balance sheets look strained, those that generated far more cash internally than they raised from equity and debt markets over three years are only nominally distressed, and the market's failure to distinguish them from genuinely market-dependent firms creates positive abnormal returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio
REASONING: The ratio of internal cash generation to total external capital raised is a single non-separable quantity spanning both themes and both external channels, and it is not the inverse of any tested leg because no archive signal has placed operating cash flow in the numerator against combined equity-and-debt issuance. Centering the leg lets the illiquidity moderator amplify both tails symmetrically, which is the only construction in this archive that has ever allowed a sign to be carried by the financing variable rather than by the distress main effect.

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Cumulative equity funding gap under liquidity deficit
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(TS_SUM(sstk, 3), TS_SUM(oancf, 3)), at)), SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(che, lct)), NEG(RATIO(wcap, at))))
HYPOTHESIS: External dependence should be measured net of what the business produced: raising a lot while also generating cash is not dependence, whereas raising a lot while burning cash is a true funding gap, and such gaps are most dangerous for firms whose working capital is already negative.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
REASONING: The signed numerator is the substantive idea — it separates opportunistic issuers from cash-consuming ones, a distinction no evaluated signal makes since gen-0's single-year net-financing test was dominated by payout terms and a loss-streak multiplier — and scaling by total assets removes the sign-flipping denominator the critic identified while keeping severe gaps at the extreme. Pairing it with the wcap-inclusive moderator, which has produced the archive's largest alphas, targets the joint objective directly.
